시장 상인이 당신을 알아본다. 그날 소리쳐 알려 준 덕에 값을 덜 잃었다: A market merchant recognizes you. They say that thanks to you shouting a warning that day, they didn't lose as much value. The merchant silently hands over an item from their stall.
It was a more useful item than I thought.
The merchant shrugged and called for the next customer.
비 오는 날 호송을 맡았던 일행에게서 소식이 온다. 당신이 앞장서 길을: News arrives from the group you escorted on a rainy day. They say they reached their destination safely thanks to you leading the way. Now, they offer to lead the way for you.
It was a wet path, but this time you could walk behind. Your breathing felt much easier.
그들은 고개를 숙이고 돌아갔다. 빚이라고 생각하지 않는 것이 서로 편했다: They bowed their heads and left. It was easier for both sides not to consider it a debt.
비 오는 날 호송에서 뒤만 따라 걸었던 일이 떠오른다. 그때 앞장섰던 사: You recall the rainy day escort where you only followed behind. They say the person who led the way back then returned injured. The rumor has only just reached your ears.
그는 괜찮다고 했지만 한쪽 어깨를 오래 문질렀다. 오래 앉아 있다 돌아왔: He said he was fine, but he rubbed one shoulder for a long time. You left after sitting for a while.
It became a forgotten matter. It only comes to mind occasionally on rainy days.
오래전 답장을 보냈던 사람에게서 다시 편지가 왔다. 필체는 그대로인데 봉: A letter arrived again from someone you wrote back to long ago. The handwriting is the same, but the envelope is worn. In that time, both the City and you have changed a lot.
There wasn't much to say. Just regards, the weather, and a name.
You did not write a reply. Instead, you placed the letter in the driest drawer.
서랍을 정리하다 오래전 넣어 둔 편지를 찾았다. 봉투는 누렇게 변했고,: While tidying the drawer, you found a letter put away long ago. The envelope has turned yellow, and you don't even know if the person you would write to is still there.
There was a brief regard in the last line. It was a regard that would no longer reach anyone.
You will read it someday. It’s just that that "someday" never comes.
게시판에 낯익은 전단이 또 붙었다. 몇 해 전 쫓아가 잡았던 사람의 일행: A familiar flyer is posted on the bulletin board again. They say it's an associate of the person you chased and caught a few years ago. The bounty is larger than last time.
The face on the flyer slowly turned around at the end of the alley. It seemed they were waiting.
신고했던 골목: The alley where you reported it
신고만 하고 지나쳤던 골목에서 누군가 당신을 알아본다. 전단 속 얼굴의: Someone recognizes you in the alley where you once just made a report and passed by. It's an acquaintance of the face on the flyer. Their gaze is not kind.
상대는 한참 노려보다 먼저 시선을 돌렸다. 돈 몇 푼을 쥐여 주고 사라졌: The other person stared for a long while before looking away first. They shoved a few coins into your hand and disappeared.
You were grabbed by the collar. You barely managed to escape.
You took a long way around. The gaze from behind followed you to the very end.
예전에 사들인 유품과 같은 각인이 있는 칼집을 든 사람이 찾아온다. 주인: A person carrying a scabbard with the same engraving as a keepsake you bought a long time ago comes looking for you. They say they are the owner's family. You could return it if they pay the price.
The family member silently took the scabbard and held it to their chest. You decided not to accept payment.
You handed it over to someone who offered the full price. The family member stood there for a long time before leaving.
골목 시장에서 예전에 지나쳤던 유품이 다시 나왔다. 그때보다 값이 많이: A keepsake you passed by before has appeared in the alley market again. The price has dropped significantly since then. It seems no one bought it.
Your eye for it was right this time. After reselling it, the price went up.
Even after haggling, it was a fake.
You never touched the belongings of the dead until the end.
밤새 일손을 거들었던 공방에서 사람이 찾아온다. 주인이 장비 한 번 손봐: Someone from the workshop where you helped out overnight comes looking for you. The owner says they will fix your gear once.
The owner was a person of few words, but their hands were precise. The gear you received back felt light.
Instead, the owner left an envelope of money, saying it was for that day's work.
하청 일손을 사양했던 공방이 문을 닫았다는 소문이 들린다. 주인은 어디론: Rumor has it that the workshop that declined your subcontracting help has closed its doors. They say the owner left for somewhere.
A single tool remained on the dust-covered workbench.
It was just a path you were passing through.
인파 속에서 같은 얼굴이 다시 지나간다. 오래전 말을 걸어 보았던 그 얼: The same face passes by again in the crowd. It is that face you tried speaking to long ago. This time, the other person stops walking first.
It was a short greeting, but you confirmed that you were both in the same City.
A nod was returned. That was enough.
인파 속에서 낯익은 얼굴이 다시 보인다. 오래전 고개를 숙이고 지나친 그: A familiar face is seen again in the crowd. It is that face that bowed and passed by long ago. It seems they recognized you too.
The other person looked surprised but soon smiled. A few trivial words were exchanged.
You passed the same path in the same way.
어느 날 여러 사람이 당신 이름을 기억하고 있다는 걸 알게 된다. 병원: One day, you realize that many people remember your name. There are people nodding in front of the hospital, at the market, and at the end of the alley. Faces whose names you don't know are mixed in.
Greetings invited more greetings. Your steps felt light all year long.
모른 척 지나간다: Pass by pretending not to notice
You hurried your steps out of awkwardness. Still, the gaze behind your back was warm.
한때 가까웠던 얼굴이 인사를 받지 않는다. 당신이 한 일이 어디선가 말이: A face that was once close does not return your greeting. It seems what you did is being talked about somewhere.
An awkward conversation was exchanged. Nothing was resolved, but the connection wasn't broken.
No answer came back. All that remained in your hands was the cold air.
You left the cold hands cold. One familiar face has been lost.
지나친 일들이 하나씩 떠오르는 밤이 있다. 잘못이라고 할 만한 것은 아니: There are nights when the things you passed by come to mind one by one. They aren't exactly mistakes. Still, memory is as accurate as a ledger.
다음 날 한 번쯤은 나선다: Step out at least once the next day
You helped with a small matter in the alley. One line in the ledger changed.
Sleep came. The ledger remains the same.
어제까지 있던 가게의 간판이 오늘은 없다. 벽에는 간판 모양으로 덜 바랜: The sign of the shop that was there until yesterday is gone today. Only a less-faded mark in the shape of the sign remains on the wall. In this City, shops and people disappear like this.
자국을 한참 본다: Look at the mark for a long time
이름은 몰라도 그 가게의 냄새는 기억났다. 기억이 있는 한 완전히 사라진: Even if you didn't know the name, you remembered the scent of that shop. As long as there is memory, it hasn't completely disappeared.
옆집 주인이 대답했다. 이 도시에서는 묻는 쪽이 더 오래 산다. 사례 삼: The owner next door answered. In this City, the one who asks lives longer. You handed them a small amount of money as a token of thanks.
골목 끝에 새 비석이 서 있다. 이름 칸은 비어 있고, 아래에는 이렇게만: A new tombstone stands at the end of the alley. The name space is empty, and below it, only this is written: For those whom this City remembers.
손을 얹고 눈을 감는다: Place your hand on it and close your eyes
The tombstone was cold. A moment later, something inside you settled down.
이름 칸에 내 이름을 새긴다: Carve your name in the name space
칼끝이 돌에 닿는 소리가 멀리까지 갔다. 이름은 새겼지만, 비석에 새겨진: The sound of the blade tip touching the stone traveled far. You carved your name, but they say the name carved on a tombstone is the first to be forgotten.
There are too many tombstones in this City that have no business being here.
어린 얼굴이 문 앞에 서서 당신의 이름을 부른다. 누구에게서 이름을 들었: A young face stands before the door and calls your name. They do not say who told them your name. They only mimic the way you hold your blade.
아이는 한 번 보고 따라 했다. 가르치는 동안 당신도 오래 잊었던 동작: The child watched once and followed suit. While teaching, you recovered a move you had long forgotten.
The child bowed their head and left. Muddy footprints remained on the threshold for a long time.
아이의 칼은 가벼웠지만 곧았다. 몇 합 뒤 당신 쪽이 먼저 손을 거두었다: The child's blade was light but straight. After a few exchanges, you were the first to lower your weapon.
The child's blade grazed your arm. It had been a long time since you felt like laughing.
오래전 함께 일하던 이의 유품 상자가 도착했다. 보낸 사람 이름은 없고,: A box of keepsakes from someone you worked with long ago has arrived. There is no sender's name, only your name written on the box.
안에는 낡은 장갑과 접힌 지도가 있었다. 지도에는 아직 가지 못한 골목이: Inside were worn gloves and a folded map. The map marks alleys you have yet to visit.
열지 않은 상자는 오래 그대로 있다. 열지 않았기에 아직 그 사람은 어딘: The unopened box has remained the same for a long time. Because it was never opened, it feels as if that person is still out there somewhere.
The smoke rose straight up. That is a rare sight in this City.
시장 사람들이 당신을 보면 말을 멈춘다. 가격표는 있지만 값은 사람마다: The market people stop talking when they see you. There are price tags, but the price changes depending on the person. This City sells things at a higher price to those who have lived here longer.
Between folding and unfolding two fingers, the price was cut in half.
The merchant smiled and doubled the price.
The market is not honest, but it saves time.
Walking away empty-handed is also a skill.
벽에 붙은 현상 전단 속 얼굴이 낯익다. 눈매가 닮았다. 아니, 정확히는: The face on the wanted poster on the wall looks familiar. The eyes are similar. No, to be precise, they are the eyes you saw in the mirror.
The paper was unexpectedly thick. There was a note from someone on the back.
A name posted by someone else should be removed by someone else.
전단을 붙인 자를 찾는다: Find the person who posted it
골목 그림자 속에서 풀칠한 손을 찾아냈다. 그 손은 아무 말 없이 도망쳤: You found the glue-stained hands in the shadows of an alley. The hands ran away without a word.
The shadow moved first. You missed them.
한 구역이 소리도 없이 가라앉고 있다. 사람들이 짐을 들고 지나간다. 누: A district is sinking without a sound. People pass by carrying their luggage. No one asks why.
You carried it until your wrists ached. Your shoulders grew a step stronger.
There were a few useful things left in the house. If you stay too long, the ceiling will collapse.
You watched until the district completely sank. Only dust remained in your eyes.
낯익은 그림자가 당신 앞을 막는다. 오래전 도운 이거나 오래전 외면한 이: A familiar shadow blocks your path. It is someone you helped long ago, or someone you turned away long ago. The shadow speaks: they have come to settle the score.
빚이 있다면 갚는다: Pay the debt if you owe one
The shadow nodded. As the price was paid, your body felt lighter.
The shadow laughed. In this City, saying you have no debt is the oldest joke.
The shadow passed by. The settlement was postponed.
경비가 교대하는 시간이다. 모든 골목에서 한꺼번에 발소리가 멈춘다. 이: It is time for the guards to change shifts. Footsteps stop in every alley all at once. This City breathes in a steady rhythm.
You went the furthest during this short gap. No one saw you.
All the guards looked like they had the same face. You shouldn't make eye contact for too long.
Waiting is also a job. In this City, they call it a break.
손가락의 연락책이 새 지령서를 내민다. 지령서의 끝은 비어 있다. 끝이: A contact from the Fingers hands you a new directive. The end of the directive is blank. They say there are no more directives with an end.
첫 줄을 읽자마자 몸이 알아서 움직였다. 이 일에는 이름이 없고 값만 있: As soon as you read the first line, your body moved on its own. This job has no name, only a price.
The contact stood there and waited. Their expression suggested that refusal was also part of the directive.
지령서의 빈 곳에 내 답을 적는다: Write your answer in the blank space of the directive
당신이 적은 글이 지령서 아래로 스며들었다. 다음 지령부터는 문체가 달라: The words you wrote seeped into the directive. From the next directive on, the writing style had changed.
어디선가 낮은 소리가 들린다. 말은 아닌데 뜻은 안다. 도시가 한 번 숨: A low sound is heard from somewhere. It is not speech, but you understand the meaning. It is the sound of the City catching its breath.
소리 안에 당신의 이름이 있었다. 부르는 것인지 세는 것인지는 알 수 없: Your name was within the sound. You cannot tell if it is calling you or counting you.
Even after the sound stopped, your hand did not leave your ear for a long time.
The sound circled a district and returned to where it started. In the meantime, your feet became lighter.
젊은 해결사가 당신에게 묻는다. 이렇게 오래 사는 법이 뭡니까. 대답하기: A young Fixer asks you: How do you live so long? Before you can answer, his eyes are fixed on the tip of your blade.
Most of what you said was a lie. Still, that Fixer lived a long time.
It was an honest answer. The Fixer turned away with a disappointed look.
칼을 쥐고 겨뤄 보자고 한다: Draw your blade and suggest a spar
가르치는 것과 시험하는 것은 같은 일이다. 몇 합 뒤 해결사가 먼저 고개: Teaching and testing are the same thing. After a few exchanges, the Fixer was the first to bow his head.
The Fixer's blade grazed you. You saw his lips move to apologize first.
It is the day to organize the documents that have piled up over a long time. Each document is a year. As you read, some years are left with only a name.
The ashes flew away lightly. Your body remembers only what it needs to remember.
You read for a long time. There were many things that were never written down.
The number of names you set aside was unexpectedly small. That is why you look at them for longer.
골목 의자에 늙은 해결사가 앉아 있다. 오래된 칼은 무릎 위에 올려 두고: An old Fixer sits on a chair in the alley. He has an old blade resting on his knees. When your eyes meet, he nods. In this City, it is a signal recognized by those who have paid the same price.
There were not many words. You looked in the same direction until the sun set.
늙은 해결사는 칼을 내밀었다. 칼날에 새겨진 숫자는 당신의 연차보다 많았: The old Fixer held out his blade. The numbers engraved on the blade were greater than your years of experience.
It was the most appropriate greeting for each other.
의뢰서의 머리말은 마지막이라고 적혀 있다. 이 도시에서 마지막은 다음 의: The header of the request says it is the final one. In this City, "final" only means "until the next request arrives."
마지막이라는 말은 값을 올려 받는 데 쓰였다. 일은 쉽지 않았지만 끝은: The word "final" was used to drive up the price. The job wasn't easy, but the ending was clean.
The folded request had been in the drawer for a long time. The next request arrived right on time.
의뢰인은 이미 자리에 없었다. 책상 위에는 마지막이 아닌 의뢰서만 쌓여: The client was already gone. On the desk, only requests that weren't the "final" one were piled up.
지도 한 장을 펼쳤더니 낯선 구역이 그려져 있다. 지도에 없던 길이 생겼: I unfolded a map to find an unfamiliar area drawn on it. They say a path that wasn't on the map has appeared. No, it’s that an erased path has been revived.
I found an old well where the map pointed. The water was clear.
Every path on the map is more unfamiliar than the one I am walking now.
The line you drew changed the City by one stroke. You decided to believe that.
계절이 바뀌는 것을 알려 주는 건 이 도시에서 혈흔 색깔이다. 올해는 짙: In this City, it is the color of bloodstains that tells us the seasons are changing. This year, it's on the darker side.
My hands were scrubbed for a long time. In the process, my hands felt lighter.
Footprints were left clearly behind. The one chasing me will be pleased.
Waiting until the color changes is also a method.
쓰러진 괴수에게서 떨어진 조각 하나가 아직 희미하게 맥박친다. 쥐면 따뜻: A fragment that fell from the fallen monster still pulses faintly. It is warm when held, and vanishes when let go.
The fragment embedded itself into my hand. It didn't hurt. A few days later, the wound was gone.
The fragment shattered without a sound. My ears felt muffled for a moment.
The collector gave the fragment a name. The price was determined by that name.
광장에 전광판이 켜져 있다. 올해의 위협 등급이 한 줄씩 지나간다. 맨: The display board in the plaza is lit. This year's threat levels scroll by line by line. Your name flickers on the bottom line.
After watching for a while, the name disappeared. The vanished name will appear somewhere else.
The plaza went quiet. The quiet plaza felt even noisier.
이름 아래에 적힌 숫자를 읽는다: Read the number written under the name
Your number was still rising. There is no end to the rising number.
부서진 구역이 다시 올라간다. 사람들은 벽돌을 나른다. 이 도시는 늘 부: The destroyed district is being rebuilt. People carry bricks. This City is always being destroyed and always being rebuilt.
I carried them until my shoulders burned. It was a long day.
One wall was raised with your money. No name was left behind.
I stood for a long time watching the wall go up.
가게 구석에 오래된 거울이 걸려 있다. 비친 얼굴은 당신이 기억하는 것보: An old mirror hangs in the corner of the shop. The face reflected is a bit more unfamiliar than the one you remember. Still, the eyes are the same.
거울 속 눈이 먼저 시선을 거두었다. 이 도시에서 오래 산다는 것은 그런: The eyes in the mirror looked away first. That is what it means to live a long time in this City.
Beneath the dust, an even older face appeared. That face, too, was one I knew.
거울을 등지고 걷는다: Turn your back to the mirror and walk
The mirror shook once behind my back.
가족 식사 · 상석: Family meal · Head of the table
큰 상의 맨 안쪽 자리가 비어 있다. 모두가 당신이 앉기를 기다린다. 형: The seat at the very end of the large table is empty. Everyone is waiting for you to sit. The elders have raised their glasses, and the youngest cannot lift their heads.
상석에 앉는다: Sit at the head of the table
당신이 잔을 들자 상이 한꺼번에 움직였다. 자리에는 무게가 있었고, 그: As you raised your glass, the table moved in unison. The seat had a weight to it, and that weight settled onto your shoulders.
One of the youngest dropped their spoon. You pretended not to notice and picked up the same side dish. The head of the table remained empty, but the meal that day stayed warm longer than usual.
집의 빈 방: The empty room in the house
집에 방이 하나 늘어 있다. 지은 적 없는 방인데 {배우자}의 물건이 가: There is an extra room in the house. It’s a room I never built, yet{배우자}'s belongings are neatly arranged inside. When I asked{배우자}, they said the room was there from the beginning. It is strange that the words don't sound like a lie.
의자 하나가 놓여 있었다. 앉으니 오래 쓴 몸에 꼭 맞았다. 문틈으로 {: A chair was placed there. Sitting in it, it fit my long-worn body perfectly. Through the crack in the door,{배우자}'s voice reached me a beat late.
쓸 만한 것을 몇 개 챙겼다. {배우자}는 아무 말 없이 방문을 닫아 주: I took a few useful things.{배우자}closed the door without a word.
불꽃은 크지 않았다. 이 자리에서는 지우는 것이 남기는 것보다 오래 간다: The flames were not large. In this place, erasing something lasts longer than leaving it behind.{배우자}watched the flames for a long time.
집에 방이 하나 늘어 있다. 지은 적 없는 방이다. 안에는 먼저 떠난 {: There is an extra room in the house. It’s a room I never built. Inside, the belongings of the departed{배우자}remain exactly as they were. It seems someone has been cleaning it continuously.
의자 하나가 놓여 있었다. 앉으니 오래 쓴 몸에 꼭 맞았다. 어디선가 {: A chair was placed there. Sitting in it, it fit my long-worn body perfectly. It felt as if{배우자}'s name had been called from somewhere.
I took a few useful things. My hand was a bit slow to close the door as I left.
불꽃은 크지 않았다. 이 자리에서는 지우는 것이 남기는 것보다 오래 간다: The flames were not large. In this place, erasing something lasts longer than leaving it behind.
집에 방이 하나 늘어 있다. 지은 적 없는 방인데 문은 열려 있고 안은: There is an extra room in the house. It’s a room I never built, but the door is open and the inside is tidy. It seems someone has been cleaning it continuously.

The drawer was filled with several identical requests. Only the locations were different.
They never came. The day spent waiting allowed your body to rest.
서랍 깊숙한 곳에서 낡은 급수 배지가 나온다. 어느 급이었는지 이제는 읽: An old Grade badge is found deep in the drawer. It is no longer legible which grade it was. In this place, a Fixer is not defined by their grade, but by the fact that they are still standing.
배지를 가슴에 단다: Pin the badge to your chest
The badge sat on your chest with an aged weight. After pinning it on, your posture straightened slightly.
The polished badge reflected your face like a mirror. It had been a long time since you saw your own face.
As you closed the drawer, the badge rang once. It was the sound of someone remembering you from afar.
협회의 마지막 서류: The last document from the Association
협회에서 서류가 한 통 왔다. 어느 건물에서 보냈는지, 이 자리까지 어떻: A document arrived from the Association. No one knows which building sent it or how it reached this place. There is no date written on it. In this place, Association documents are the only record that tells you what day it is.
The document vanished the moment you signed it. Only your name remained with the Association. You felt a little more secure.
읽는 동안 글자가 한 줄씩 늘었다. 끝까지 읽으면 오래 살게 되는 문서: While reading, the text grew by a line. It felt like a document that would grant a long life if read to the end.
The ashes floated in the shape of letters for a moment before settling.
날개의 낡은 깃: An old feather from a Wing
집 문틈에 낡은 깃이 끼어 있다. 소속 날개의 문장이 새겨져 있다. 날개: An old feather is caught in the door crack. The crest of a Wing is engraved on it. A Wing is a place that cannot reach this location, yet the feather arrived first. The sender is nowhere to be seen.
The feather grew warm the moment you grasped it. The sensation of belonging to an organization for a long time returned to your arm.
깃을 창가에 꽂아 둔다: Place the feather on the windowsill
창가의 깃은 바람이 없는데 흔들렸다. 날개가 멀리서 안부를 묻는 것 같다: The feather on the windowsill swayed despite the lack of wind. It felt as if the Wing was asking after you from afar.
When you returned the feather to the door crack, it was gone by the next day.
서열이 있는 곳의 사람이 집 앞에서 서서 인사만 하고 간다. 일을 시키러: Someone from a place with a hierarchy stands before the house, offers a greeting, and leaves. They say they didn't come to assign work, but to ask how you are. In this place, hierarchy remains as a greeting.
답을 들은 사람은 고개를 숙이고 갔다. 몸이 조직의 박에 오랜만에 맞았다: The person who heard your reply bowed their head and left. For the first time in a while, your body matched the rhythm of an organization.
A small bundle was left where they had sat to drink tea.
문 너머에서 한참 기다리는 기척이 났다. 기척이 사라질 때까지 문을 열지: There was a presence waiting for a long time on the other side of the door. You did not open it until the presence vanished.
사무소 인장이 우편함에 들어 있다. 이름 칸이 비어 있는 인장이다. 이: A workshop seal is in the mailbox. It is a seal with an empty space for a name. In this place, workshop work means receiving no work from anyone. Still, the seal looks for a place to be pressed.
The name of the workshop appeared where you stamped it. It was not work that was prepared, but a place.
인장을 서랍에 넣는다: Put the seal in the drawer
인장은 서랍 속에서 한 번 눌린 소리를 냈다. 일이 하나 처리된 것 같다: The seal made a sound as if it had been pressed once inside the drawer. It felt like a task had been processed.
인장을 문에 걸어 둔다: Hang the seal on the door
The seal hanging on the door swayed without wind. Those who come and go will recognize it.
엄지에서 오래 지키던 약속이 이 자리까지 따라왔다. 약속은 형태가 없고: A promise long kept by the Thumb has followed you to this place. The promise has no form, only weight. In this place, a promise does not vanish even if it is not kept.
The renewed promise pulsed like a heartbeat within your body. Your body grew firmer with its weight.
The released promise swayed once and then settled. Your shoulders felt lighter.
The promise you kept was warm. It is the only warm thing in this place.
검지에서 오던 지령이 끊어진 지 오래인데 오늘은 한 장이 도착했다. 글씨: It has been a long time since the directives from the Index stopped, but one arrived today. The handwriting is familiar, but the content changes every time you read it. It seems the ones issuing the directives are also experiencing the displacement of this place.
따른 지령은 끝나기도 전에 다음 지령으로 이어졌다. 몸이 알아서 움직이게: The directive you followed led to the next one before it even ended. Your body began to move on its own.
고친 글자가 한 줄 남고 나머지는 사라졌다. 이 자리에서 지령은 합의가: One line of the corrected text remained, and the rest vanished. In this place, a directive becomes an agreement.
The unread directive grew old on the windowsill. The older it got, the softer it became.
문고리에 사슬이 감겨 있다. 중지의 사슬이다. 끊으려 하면 풀리고 풀려: A chain is wrapped around the door handle. It is a chain of the Middle. If you try to break it, it loosens; if you try to loosen it, it tightens. What cannot be let go of even in this place is the act of not letting go of each other.
The chain grew quiet while wrapped around your arm. The weight pressed down on your body, making you stand all the straighter.
The released chain made a sound on the ground once and vanished. The spot where it disappeared was warm.
문고리째 둔다: Leave it on the door handle
The chain rang slightly every time you opened the door. After a long time, it sounded like a clock.
약지에서 맞춘 반지가 서랍에서 나왔다. 어느 쪽 손가락에도 맞지 않는데: A ring tailored by the Ring appeared in the drawer. It doesn't fit any finger, but when you put it on, it fits. In this place, "fitting" is not a matter of shape, but of the time you have held onto it.
The moment you put it on, the ring clung to your finger. It soaked into your body like a long-worn garment.
반지를 창가에 둔다: Place the ring on the windowsill
The ring on the windowsill sparkled once every time the sun set.
There was no one to hand it to. The mere gesture of trying to hand it over made your heart quiet.
집 앞길 끝에 공방 주인이 와 있다. 도시의 거리에서 가게를 열던 사람이: The workshop owner is standing at the end of the path in front of the house. They are someone who used to run a shop on the streets of the City. They say they dragged their luggage all the way here. Not because there were no customers left in the City, but because they needed a customer who has been standing in this place for a long time.
가게를 연다고 한다: Say you will open the shop
The owner set up a workbench by the roadside. A shop in this place stands only as much as it is needed. That shop appears when you visit the workshop district.
The luggage was light, but it felt heavy when you set it down. The owner bowed their head.
The owner looked back once and walked to the end of the path. The shop stood at the end of the road.
해결사 등록도 소속도 없는 사람이 집 앞에 서 있다. 같은 이름도, 같은: A person with no Fixer registration and no affiliation is standing in front of the house. They are not of the same name or the same path, yet they have come to this place in the same way. Both of you know that you are losing your names in this place.
차를 마신 사람이 입을 열었다. 이 자리에 온 이유를 이야기하는 동안 몸: The person who drank the tea opened their mouth. As they spoke of the reason they came to this place, your body relaxed.
Your steps were in sync. When you walked to the end of the path and returned, your body felt a little firmer.
There was a presence standing outside the door for a long time. When the sun set, the presence vanished.
